sample_unit: message triads (patient message, AI-generated draft reply, care team response)

links.outcome: Demographic differences in tone of AI-drafted patient message replies
links.effect: AI drafts had lower odds of polite language for Hispanic vs White patients. They had lower odds of positive affect for Hispanic, non-English-preferring, female-sex, and lower-area-income patients.
links.quote: AI-GDRs also had lower odds of conveying positive affect in responses to patients who were Hispanic, preferred a non-English language, assigned female sex at birth, or lived in an area with a lower average income.

links.outcome: Population-specific differences in tone of generated patient message replies
links.effect: AI drafts had lower odds of polite language for Hispanic patients than White patients. Care team responses showed some similar differences in positive affect.
links.quote: AI-GDRs had lower odds of including polite language in responses to Hispanic patients, compared to White patients.

screen.reason: Retrospective evaluation of AI-generated draft replies deployed in real clinical practice to assess demographic biases/disparities in tone.
